chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abdul Malik ibn Utba, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about the papers that accumulate; can they be burned with fire while there is something from the Mention of Allah in them? He said: No, they must be washed with water first, before (burning).
ai.seo_question: How should papers with the Name of Allah be disposed of according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the proper disposal method for 'qaratis' (sheets of paper) bearing the Name of Allah, establishing that direct burning is prohibited because the sacred text retains its sanctity. Instead, the ink must be washed off with water first, a practice rooted in the Shia principle of respecting the physical vessel of divine revelation, distinguishing it from the treatment of ordinary paper. This ruling reflects the broader jurisprudential emphasis on preserving the dignity of the Quranic text even in its fragmented or written forms.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al hakam, from Abdul Malik Bin Utba, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘

I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the papers which tend to accumulate. ‘Can they be burned with the fire and therein is something from the Mention of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No! You should wash it out with the water first, before (burning)’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from ‘Abd al-Malik ibn ‘Utbah who has said the following:

“Once I asked abu al-Hassan (a.s.) about the papers that accumulate if they can be burned in which names of Allah may also be found. The Imam said, ‘No, they must not be burned instead, first they should be washed with water.’”
